thread.title: Another Analyst Reduces Apple Stock Price Forecast

title: Another Analyst Reduces Apple Stock Price Forecast
text:
Another Analyst Reduces Apple Stock Price Forecast By Nov. 27, 2018 10:49 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Aaron Text size
RBC Capital Markets believes Apple (AAPL) may report results in its March quarter below expectations due to weaker iPhone demand.
Analyst Amit Daryanani lowered his price target for the smartphone maker to $235 from $240, citing recent iPhone supplier warnings and media reports.
“Given sustained datapoints around soft iPhone demand from supply-chain and others, we think its prudent to adjust estimates lower, especially as it relates to Mar-qtr and beyond,” he wrote on Tuesday. “We think investors will wait for datapoints/noise level to stabilize before getting more positive on the name (dynamic we think should occur in early 2019).”
Apple stock is down 0.8% to $173.22 on Tuesday.
The analyst reduced his Apple March-quarter earnings-per-share estimate to $2.98 from $3.03, versus the $3.01 Wall Street consensus.
Last week, The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Apple has cut orders in recent weeks for all three newly released iPhone models.
Apple stock has fallen more than 20% this month as investors grow increasingly worried about iPhone sales . Newsletter Sign-up
Earlier this month, wireless chip maker Qorvo (QRVO) reduced its financial guidance for its third quarter, citing weaker demand for high-end smartphones. And iPhone suppliers Lumentum Holdings (LITE) and Japan Display (6740.Japan) lowered their financial forecasts on Nov. 12.
Despite the negative news flow, Daryanani is still optimistic about Apple shares for the long term and reaffirmed his Outperform rating for the stock.
“We think that in an increasingly ‘risk-off’ environment, AAPL with its strong balance sheet, aggressive buyback, and ability to drive [gross margins] higher remains a core large-cap tech holding,” he wrote.
